In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RB/p130 is a major tumor suppressor in lung cancer, while the RBL1/p105 and RBL2 proteins are not.
RB inactivation occurs in 90.4% of small cell lung cancer, but is a rare event in other lung tumors and mesotheliomas.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RB is mutated in 90% of SCLC and 11% of non-SCLC, RBL1 and/or RBL2 is mutated in 0% of SCLCs and non-SCLC.
RB mutations in SCLC, and p16 mutations in non-SCLC, are the only common mutations in this family.
the RB family of tumor suppressors is not a common target in lung cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RBL1 and p130 are expressed and functional in lung cancer.
RBL1 and RB2 are not inactivated in human lung tumors, which is in contrast to recent reports.
the RB-related genes are not mutated in the vast majority of lung tumors and that the RBL1 and RB2 gene family may not be important targets for inactivation in this disease.
